paper_title: Chiplet Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithm Based on Communication Consumption and Temperature

scenario.description: Multi-window display (MWD) system with 12 chiplets mapped onto a 2.5-D IC with passive interposer. Chiplet sizes range from 2.5×2.5 mm (blend) to 8.0×6.0 mm (nr). Power values range from 5 W (blend) to 70 W (mem2). System uses mesh topology on grid with ambient temperature 318.5 K, heat spreader 5 mm edge, heatsink 20 mm edge, fin-channel heatsink with 30 mm fin height, 1 mm fin width, 10 cm fan radius at 5000 RPM. Hotspot 7.0 thermal simulator models the passive silicon interposer with six layers: organic substrate, C4 bump layer, silicon interposer, microbump layer, chiplet layout, and TIM. Communication task graph shows bandwidth ranging from 256 Mbit/s (mem3) to 64 Mbit/s (mem1, blend). Algorithm CMO optimizes chiplet placement to minimize peak temperature and inter-chiplet communication consumption simultaneously using weight factor α.
scenario.architecture: 2.5-D IC with passive silicon interposer; 12 chiplets on mesh topology; six-layer packaging: organic substrate (FR-4), C4 bumps, silicon interposer with through-silicon vias (TSVs), microbumps, chiplets, thermal interface material (TIM), copper spreader, and air-forced fin-channel heatsink
scenario.workload: Multi-window display (MWD) multimedia application; static power distribution over chiplets; communication task graph with peak bandwidth 256 Mbit/s between mem3 and hs; communication priorities mapped in communication priority list (CPL)
scenario.operating_point: Ambient temperature 318.5 K; forced convection cooling with lateral airflow from heatsink side; fan speed 5000 RPM; thermal design uses realistic air-forced heatsink with fin geometry and forced convection model; initial layout: peak temperature 381.41 K, communication consumption 1026.72 µJ; optimized layout (α=0.5): peak temperature 373.58 K, communication consumption 794.59 µJ

original_setup.benchmark: Multi-window display (MWD) system with 12 IP cores

physical_mismatches.reason: Hotspot 7.0 uses compact thermal resistance/capacitance circuit model with fourth-order Runge-Kutta adaptive stepping; does not model transient chiplet power variations or dynamic frequency scaling

Algorithm assumes uniform power distribution over chiplet area and that surface temperature equals overall temperature due to assumed high thermal conductivity and thinness; ignores within-chiplet thermal gradients
Manhattan distance metric used for heuristic calculation; actual thermal resistance between chiplets depends on interposer thermal properties and TSV distribution which are not spatially detailed
Communication consumption calculation uses static communication task graph; does not account for runtime variation or dynamic task mapping

studio_assumptions: Chiplet power is uniformly distributed across chiplet area
Chiplet surface temperature equals overall chiplet temperature due to high thermal conductivity
Passive interposer with back-end-of-line process; six-layer packaging stack is fixed
Through-silicon vias (TSVs) provide thermal and electrical coupling between chiplets and substrate
Air-forced heatsink with fin-channel geometry provides forced convection cooling; fan speed fixed at 5000 RPM
Thermal interface material (TIM) provides specified thermal resistance between chips and spreader
Manhattan distance between chiplet midpoints represents inter-chiplet thermal coupling strength
Communication energy per unit distance is constant at 0.186 pJ/bit/mm (ORION 2.0 model)
Mesh topology grid determines allowed placement positions; unit grid size derived from chiplet sizes and mandatory spacing
Chiplet placement is static after optimization; no runtime relocation
missing_inputs: No repository URL or code artifact provided for CMO algorithm implementation
No detailed HotSpot thermal model parameters (layer-specific thermal conductivity, thickness of each layer beyond spreader/heatsink dimensions)
No specification of interposer material properties or TSV density and distribution
No thermal resistance matrix or detailed coupling coefficients between chiplets
No transient power traces or workload time-varying behavior for MWD application
No validation against silicon measurements or experimental thermal imaging data
Communication task graph bandwidth values are static; no temporal profile or burstiness characterization
No specification of TIM thermal conductivity or thickness
No fin efficiency or convection coefficient model details for heatsink
Chiplet actual sizes and spacing rules are preprocessed; exact algorithm for theoretical size determination not fully specified in text
